analyst_view.overall: Early view: Alverca (11th) and Moreirense (9th) are separated by two points in mid-table. Alverca under Sérgio Ferreira lead the league in tackles and have drawn with Casa Pia and lost narrowly to Benfica and Arouca recently. Moreirense want to press higher under Vasco Botelho da Costa and could have Francisco Domingues and Kiko Bondoso back from muscle injuries by then.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. I lean slightly higher: Moreirense's games average close to three goals (13 scored, 18 conceded), and Alverca's about 2.6. Moreirense's pressing game creates chances at both ends.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.3 corners, mostly for Alverca at home. That fits two sides that win the ball in midfield rather than through long spells of pressure. I keep to the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean higher: Alverca make more tackles than any team in the league, and Moreirense's higher press will lead to plenty of challenges in midfield. Two sides fighting for every ball tend to pick up bookings.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.5 shots. Alverca's tackling breaks play up, but Moreirense's pressing produces quick attempts. I see no clear reason to move the figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.4 shots on target. Alverca's attack depends on Dawda Camara, who has not scored for over a month, while Moreirense have more ways to score. Overall I stay near the site's figure.
